blocks.title: Nested conditionals
blocks.text: Checking a condition inside another condition is called nesting: an if statement is placed inside the block of another if or else.

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
weather = "rainy"
temperature = 10
if weather == "rainy":
....if temperature < 15:
........print("Wear a raincoat")
....else:
........print("Take an umbrella")
else:
....print("Enjoy your day!")
If it is rainy and below 15 degrees, wear a raincoat; if it is only rainy, take an umbrella; if it is not rainy, just enjoy the day. With these values the program prints "Wear a raincoat".

blocks.prompt: What does the program print with weather = "rainy" and temperature = 20?
blocks.explanation: "Take an umbrella": it is rainy, but the inner condition temperature < 15 is false.

items: Nested conditionals: an if inside another if; the inner test runs only when the outer one allows it.
